title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: The real numbers \(c,\) \(b,\) \(a\) form an arithmetic sequence with \(a \geq b \geq c \geq 0.\) The quadratic \(ax^2+bx+c\) has exactly one root. What is this root?

solutions.text:
Let the common difference be \(d\), so \(c=b-d\) and \(a=b+d\).

A quadratic with exactly one real root has discriminant \(0\), so \(b^2-4ac=0\). Substituting gives \(b^2=4(b+d)(b-d)=4b^2-4d^2\), hence \(4d^2=3b^2\).

Since \(b,d\ge0\), \(2d=\sqrt3 b\). The double root is \(\frac{-b}{2a}=\frac{-b}{2(b+d)}=\frac{-1}{2+\sqrt3}=-2+\sqrt3\).

Thus, the correct answer is D .
